goal: WP1.2: ERE translator and the differential's runner

steps.description: hooks/lib/ai_ere.py, the parser (spec D3): a byte-level tokenizer over the pattern's UTF-8 bytes (C-locale semantics, H2/D6) and bracket expressions. [[:class:]] is an ASCII set, [[:space:]] is [ \t\n\v\f\r]; a backslash inside brackets is literal; []a], [^]a] and a trailing '-' are handled; single-character [[=c=]] and [[.c.]] are accepted, as range endpoints too; bad ranges, '-' as a non-final range start, a class or equivalence class as a range endpoint, unknown classes, multi-character [[.x.]]/[[=x=]] and an unterminated [ raise EreError. Tokens for the rest: escapes (GNU ops, back-references, literal escapes), anchors, groups, alternation, quantifiers and {m,n} intervals. tests/test_ere_unit.py starts with the parser cases; add tests/test-ere-unit.sh (two-line wrapper) and the run-all.sh entry. By hand: pylint --rcfile .pylintrc on both new .py files.
291 > 250: the parser's unit cases, their wrapper and the run-all entry become their own step; the parser stays in step 1

hooks/lib/ai_ere.py, translate and compile: the GNU escapes \w \W \s \S \b \B \< \> \` \' as explicit ASCII sets and lookarounds (re.ASCII); back-references \1-\9 to a completed group, emitted as (?:\N); stacked quantifiers wrapped, so a+? and a*? become (?:a+)?; '.' with DOTALL and '$' as \Z (no REG_NEWLINE); a lone ')' is literal; invalid forms compile to None, which never matches: a leading *, + , ? or {, a quantifier after an anchor, (?, a bad interval, a trailing backslash, an unmatched ( or [, a back-reference to an open or absent group; the { cases follow glibc's parse_dup_op and are left to the oracle; compiled as a bytes regex; a cache per process; Ere.search and Ere.captures (subject encoded UTF-8, captures decoded with surrogateescape). Unit cases for each, including the invalid forms (R6, unit part). By hand: pylint on the .py files.

tests/test_pattern_differential.py, the oracle and the runner (D4 ii): one long-lived bash per locale (C, C.UTF-8; a missing locale is skipped with one line) reads NUL-delimited pattern/subject records and answers through [[ $s =~ $p ]] (rc 0/1/2 = match/no match/invalid); the verdict is compared with ai_ere (None = invalid). The declared-divergence list (D6) lives inside the test. A failure names the pattern, the subject, both verdicts and the seed (AI_DIFF_SEED, default 20261003, printed). For now it covers every string of both defaults files (except _comment) over the characterization corpus: the COMMANDS array of tests/test-guard-characterization.sh read through bash, its file-tool paths from the golden labels, and every string of the fixture payloads. Without bash it skips with one line. Add tests/test-pattern-differential.sh and the run-all.sh entry. By hand: pylint on the new .py file.
3 review findings: #2 stacked quantifiers merged into one; #3 stack-dependent None not cached; #4 DECLARED [[.x.]] entry dropped. #1 goes to WP1.3

open_risks: review #1 (MEDIUM, WP1.3 decision): glibc never matches a back-reference to an empty-able group repeated with min>=2, e.g. (a*){2}\1 on aa; ai_ere does. Defaults hold no back-references.

review #2 (MEDIUM, narrowed, WP1.3 D5): only *, + and ? under a repeat fold; an interval under a repeat still backtracks exponentially, a?{2}+b 16 s and a{1,3}+b 33 s at ~35 bytes, as do (a*)*b and (a+)+b. No timeout until D5.
review #3 residual: patterns nested deeper than ~190 groups exceed Python's recursion limit and give None (never matches) though glibc accepts them; no longer cached. Depth limit for the spec owner.

tooling: remediate sets no tree_before, so step-done measures a remediation from the task's base tree; R1 closed with --force (known-risks.md). glibc's oracle can spin on a stack before \1 (known-risks.md).
